newsitem.title: USA: Tee-Comm sees cost key to satellite profit.
newsitem.headline: Tee-Comm sees cost key to satellite profit.

text.p: Satellite television company Tee-Comm Electronics Inc on Wednesday said it expects its low operating costs will make it a profitable player in an increasingly crowded market dominated by big spenders.
"We believe we will succeed, based on our low operating costs," Jim Wilkinson, Chief Operating Officer, told an investment conference.
Canadian-based Tee-Comm is fighting PrimeStar, DirecTV and EchoStar Communications Corp and later this year will be up against News Corp Ltd's ASkyB.
PrimeStar is owned by a consortium including Tele-Communications Inc. DirectTV is owned by Hughes Electronics Corp and AT&T Corp has a small stake.
Tee-Comm's AlphaStar service has been operational for four months, has 40,000 U.S. subscribers and is awaiting approval for its Canadian license.
"We expect a decision on that shortly," Wilkinson said.

The company has so far gained average gross revenues per subscriber of $42 per month against an industry range of $31 to $36 per month. After costs of service provision, net revenues work out at $15.37 per month, the company said.
"That gives us a breakeven point of 500,000 subscribers, which we expect to reach by late 1998," Wilkinson said.
He said many rivals have said they are predicting that they need 1.3 - 1.4 million subscribers to breakeven.
The company is targeting niche markets in the ethnic communities in North America and will launch Spanish and French language channels shortly.
It has 115 channels in the U.S. and 70 channels broadcast in a test mode in Canada pending the license decision.
The company is also targeting homes that have no cable TV or little and city areas where there is cable TV congestion.
"We have spent $130 million to build this service; everyone else spent at least $1 billion to get there," Wilkinson said.

The company manages to keep costs down by leasing rather than owning assets. In May, it will move its service to AT&T's Telstar 5 satellite from AT&T's 402R satellite, which will give it more channels and allow the company to broadcast all the way from northern Canada to the northern fringes of South America.
